book_title: Making Websites Win: Apply the Customer-Centric Methodology That Has Doubled the Sales of Many Leading Websites

frameworks.name: Diagnosis-first remedy selection (DiPS, lock and key)
frameworks.decision: Which change to make on a page or funnel step, and whether a proposed best-practice remedy (testimonials, guarantee, urgency, new headline) is warranted at all.
evidence_required: At least one diagnosis source naming why people stall (user-test notes, buyer 'nearly stopped' answers, exit survey, sales/support/chat objections, recordings) with counts n of N
The page or step and its single goal
Traffic source and awareness stage (from conversion-audit step 1)
prerequisites: Goal defined (book: optimise for the content's reason to exist)
Owner-confirmed facts for any counter-objection copy

branches.if: Visitors cannot say what the product does
branches.then: Plain description of what it does, early; do not add guarantee, discount or testimonials first

branches.if: They understand it but not why they need it
branches.then: Benefits tied to features they care about

branches.if: They doubt it works
branches.then: Proof: features, data, demonstrations, named reviews

branches.if: Compatibility or fit questions dominate
branches.then: Specific compatibility details where the question arises

branches.if: Price feels too high among qualified buyers
branches.then: Justify price (value comparison, what is included) or change the offer (BK13-K7)

branches.if: They distrust the company
branches.then: Credibility proof (size, reviews, press, associations) (BK13-K3 trust branch)

branches.if: They will think about it
branches.then: Genuine reasons to act now, or an intermediate step for the not-ready (BK13-K8)

branches.if: No diagnosis evidence exists
branches.then: Run the cheapest feasible diagnosis (BK13-K2) before recommending remedies; only observable blockers (broken form, missing price for price-shoppers) go to fix-now

branches.if: A requested remedy's function does not match any diagnosed problem
branches.then: Advise against it as clutter; put it under 'Later' or drop it

steps: State the page goal and audience
Collect diagnosis evidence (BK13-K2)
Code each reason into a problem class with counts
Pick the most frequent or most blocking class
Choose a remedy whose function matches it
Place the counter where and when the objection arises
Measure with the feasible method (BK13-K4); re-diagnose if the signal does not move
exceptions_failure_modes: Few respondents make the top class unstable
Several problems co-exist; fixing one can surface the next
Buyers' answers miss barriers that stopped everyone else
A diagnosis is a hypothesis, not a proven cause
Remedies add length and can bury the key message

requirements.labor: About 3-8 owner hours for 3-5 user tests or buyer calls plus coding
requirements.capability: Can run a silent task-based test and code objections; ClimbOS drafts scripts and codes notes
requirements.measurement: Goal event on the page; otherwise label results unmeasured

metrics: Share of research mentions per problem class (n of N)
Goal conversion or earlier step rate
Repeat-test signal: does the confusion or objection still appear?
guardrails: No invented proof, guarantees or urgency
Diagnoses labelled 'likely reason', never as proven cause
stop_review: Remedy shipped and the same objection still appears in the next 3-5 tests: revisit the diagnosis
Two remedies in a row fail to move the step: check whether the binding constraint is elsewhere (shared/agents/diagnosis.ts)
alternatives: No traffic: method marketing, selling face to face or by phone, VOC aggregators
No customers: competitor and adjacent reviews (voc-research)
No analytics: owner tally of enquiries and the questions asked
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: DiPS is the book's central idea and the strongest transferable rule. The existing conversion-audit skill is checklist-led (offer, proof, CTA, friction...), which is useful as a page scan but can slide into the 'marketing pharmacy' the authors criticise when no buyer evidence exists. Diagnosis remains inference; it ranks hypotheses rather than proving causes.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: every 'fix now' or 'test' item in a conversion audit names the diagnosed problem class and its evidence source with a count; items without one go to 'Later' unless they are observable blockers
proposed: recommend a guarantee or other risk reducer only when risk or credibility is among the top diagnosed problems (or the owner asks), matching its type to the concern
proposed: when no diagnosis evidence exists, output a diagnosis plan before any persuasion remedies

frameworks.climbos_location: skills/conversion-audit/SKILL.md (candidate v2: add a diagnose step before steps 4-12); shared/agents/diagnosis.ts (within-stage reason classes)

relation_to_existing.note: Versions conversion-audit (diagnosis gate and remedy-function check). Duplicates CH-C5's 'match the reducer to the dominant risk' for guarantees. Consistent with Book 10 section 6 'separate persuasion problems from usability failures'.

frameworks.disagreements: landing-pages SKILL.md:56 includes a risk-reversal section by default and line 22 suggests a guarantee when none exists; the book (and CH-C5) make guarantees conditional on diagnosed risk. Decider: diagnosed hesitation evidence; with none, the section stays optional and is labelled a suggestion.

frameworks.name: Diagnosis method selection by traffic and customer base (low-traffic toolkit)
frameworks.decision: Which research methods to use to learn why visitors do not convert, given traffic, number of reachable customers, owner time and consent basis.
evidence_required: Weekly visitors to the page (or unknown)
Number of recent buyers reachable and the consent basis
Who talks to buyers (owner, staff, resellers, support)
Owner hours available
prerequisites: Owner approval for any tool install, survey, recording or customer contact
Consent banner and PII masking before session recording where required
Permission before recording calls (book notes this)

branches.if: Pre-launch or a handful of visitors a day
branches.then: Hallway user tests (3-5), method marketing (buy and use own and competitor products, including offline analogues), sell face to face or by phone, interview VOC aggregators (sales, support, resellers), read reviews and plain-language descriptions

branches.if: Has about 10+ reachable recent buyers with a contact basis
branches.then: Ask 'what nearly stopped you' on the thank-you page or by email; run 2-3 retrospective walkthroughs with recent buyers

branches.if: Moderate traffic and owner approves tools
branches.then: Session recordings of strugglers, form-field drop-off, click/scroll maps for anomalies, site-search log review

branches.if: Expected survey answers reach the needed count inside the owner's horizon (computed)
branches.then: Exit survey (purpose / achieved? / what stopped you) or on-page survey; visitor-intention gap analysis only once about 100 answers are feasible

branches.if: Finance or health audience
branches.then: Expect low participation; plan compliance review in small chunks (micro-approvals)

branches.if: Too few answers expected
branches.then: Do not run the survey; switch to interviews, tests or aggregators

steps: Write the question the research must answer
Compute expected responses = eligible visitors x response rate (owner rate if known; the book's ~3% only as a dated placeholder)
Pick 2-3 methods from the branch, cheapest first
Draft scripts (tasks for tests; 3-question exit survey; buyer question)
Get owner approval for contact, tools and consent
Code findings into problem classes with counts
Hand the top class to BK13-K1
exceptions_failure_modes: Self-selected testers are more time-rich and cash-poor than buyers
The researcher's own method-marketing experience is one customer
Research framed as 'market research' yields polite answers
Buyer surveys miss barriers that stopped everyone
Heatmaps mostly show the obvious; only anomalies matter

requirements.cash: $0 to low (gift-card incentives, optional remote test service fees)
requirements.capability: Moderate; ClimbOS drafts tasks, questions, codes notes
requirements.measurement: Response counts and coded themes; no conversion claim

metrics: New themes per extra session (stop when none)
guardrails: Contact customers only on a lawful basis; never cold-email purchased lists
Check terms before analysing customer-to-friend messages (the book flags this)
Do not deceive testers about what is being sold
stop_review: Stop collecting when two consecutive sessions add no new theme
If expected responses for a survey fall below the needed count within the horizon, switch method
alternatives: No traffic and no customers: VOC aggregators plus competitor and adjacent reviews (voc-research)
No owner time: remote unmoderated tests (paid) if budget is approved
No tool access: owner notes of every phone or email question for 2 weeks
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: the book's most useful contribution for small businesses is its low-traffic list and the observational methods ClimbOS skills barely mention. Searching skills/*/SKILL.md found no step that runs user tests or watches recordings; voc-research is text-mining-led. The response-rate figures are dated agency numbers.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: before recommending a survey, compute expected responses in code from the owner's traffic and a stated response rate, and switch method if the needed count is out of reach within the horizon
proposed: session recording and heatmap suggestions carry a consent and masking prerequisite where privacy law applies
proposed: weight barrier evidence from recent buyers above non-buyer price complaints when choosing the first fix, while keeping non-buyer purpose data for fit questions

relation_to_existing.note: Duplicates the 'what almost/nearly stopped them' question (voc-research SKILL.md:30, CH-C2 step 1). Extends with observational methods (user tests, retrospective walkthroughs, recordings, form analytics, VOC aggregators, method marketing, selling to learn) and a response-count feasibility check.

frameworks.disagreements: Book: ask buyers, not non-buyers. voc-research leans on competitor and public reviews (mostly non-buyers of this business). Decider: purpose. For barriers among qualified prospects, weight buyers; for positioning and alternatives, public reviews are fine. CH-C2 'fewer than ~10 respondents: 3-5 interviews' agrees with the book.

frameworks.name: Problem taxonomy and prioritisation (where to work first)
frameworks.decision: Which diagnosed problem, on which page or step, to work on first; and whether conversion work should precede buying more traffic.
evidence_required: Page or step reach (share of eventual buyers or visitors who see it)
Coded problem classes with counts
Owner funnel numbers for the binding-constraint check
prerequisites: BK13-K1/K2 evidence
Diagnosis from shared/agents/diagnosis.ts showing conversion or activation is the weak link (or unknown)

branches.if: Broken flows or errors observed
branches.then: Fix immediately; no test needed (Book 10 section 6 agrees)

branches.if: Comprehension problems (unclear writing or product description)
branches.then: Fix before persuasion work; clarity is the prerequisite

branches.if: Usability struggle
branches.then: Wireframe, test on 1-2 people, iterate

branches.if: Visitors want things you do not offer
branches.then: Offer/range gap analysis (BK13-K7)

branches.if: Benefits unclear or value unmentioned
branches.then: List all value delivered; apply so-what / yeah-right rule

branches.if: Trust in company vs trust in product
branches.then: Treat separately; surface existing proof on high-traffic pages first

branches.if: Risk or skepticism
branches.then: Guarantee per BK13-K6

branches.if: Many product-specific objections
branches.then: Complex-sale structure BK13-K5

branches.if: Not ready, distracted, delaying, or handover
branches.then: BK13-K8

branches.if: Choosing competitors
branches.then: Niche or differentiate (positioning skill)

branches.if: Diagnosis says demand (reach) is binding
branches.then: Do not lead with CRO; follow the computed constraint

steps: List problems with class, evidence count and the page/step where each bites
Compute priority = reach share x mention share (proposed, code); blockers override
Prefer pages most buyers see (book: arteries; zero-traffic pages yield nothing)
Pick the top 1-3; size bold changes, not tweaks
Record each as a hypothesis with metric
exceptions_failure_modes: Mention counts reflect who you asked
Reach unknown without analytics (use owner estimates labelled)
Categories overlap (trust vs risk)
Power-law arithmetic assumes ad costs stay flat and more traffic is buyable

requirements.measurement: Analytics page reach or owner estimate

guardrails: No profit forecast from hypothetical conversion doubling
Book benchmarks not used as targets
stop_review: Top problem fixed and the step still underperforms: re-run diagnosis
Constraint shifts to another stage: move work there
alternatives: No analytics: rank by mention share only and label it
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: the book gives a taxonomy and broad priorities (high-traffic pages, frequency-ranked objections, clarity and usability first, bold changes) but no scoring rule. The reach x frequency score is a ClimbOS design, not the authors'. Book 10 section 6's understand / believe / want / complete sequence is a coarser version of the same taxonomy; the 14 classes map into it.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: order conversion fixes by blockers first, then comprehension and usability, then persuasion classes, within each by reach x mention share computed in code
proposed: show the profit leverage of a conversion change only as an owner-input scenario in economics code, labelled hypothetical, never as an expected result
proposed: do not prioritise CRO over reach when the computed binding constraint is demand

frameworks.climbos_location: skills/conversion-audit/SKILL.md step 14 (candidate v2); shared/agents/diagnosis.ts; shared/agents/economics.ts / shared/growth/calc.ts

relation_to_existing.note: conversion-audit prioritises by blocker/major/minor and fix/test/later; this adds reach x frequency and a clarity-first order. diagnosis.ts picks the weak stage but has no within-stage reason input.

frameworks.disagreements: Book: CRO is the most important activity for any business (part0015 [75]). ClimbOS diagnosis.ts decides the binding constraint from the owner's numbers and may pick demand. Decider: the owner's funnel numbers, not the book's claim.

frameworks.name: Bold changes and low-traffic measurement
frameworks.decision: Whether and how to measure a page change when traffic is small: A/B, earlier metric, pooled pages, bought traffic, user tests or labelled before/after.
evidence_required: Weekly eligible visitors
Baseline rate of the candidate metric(s)
Minimum worthwhile effect
Owner horizon
Reversibility and cost of the change
prerequisites: Change grounded in diagnosis (BK13-K1)
Conversion tracking working
Owner approval for any spend to buy traffic

branches.if: sampleSize weeks <= horizon for a bold change
branches.then: Fixed-horizon A/B in whole weeks, read once at the end, SRM check, guardrails

branches.if: Outcome metric too rare
branches.then: Use an earlier step (e.g. clicked Book) as primary, keep the outcome as guardrail (EXP-C5)

branches.if: Several similar pages each get little traffic
branches.then: Apply the same change to all and analyse pooled, with a per-page check for opposite effects

branches.if: Owner has an approved budget
branches.then: Temporarily buy traffic to the page; count it as a cost

branches.if: Still infeasible
branches.then: User tests as the measure of comprehension/usability; ship reversible fixes; before/after labelled observational

branches.if: Change is a tweak (colour, small wording)
branches.then: Do not test; ship if harmless or drop

branches.if: Owner wants a lower confidence threshold
branches.then: Allowed only if pre-registered, for reversible low-cost changes, read once at the planned end, and labelled directional; never 'incremental' wording

steps: Write the decision and minimum worthwhile effect
Run sampleSize for the outcome and for earlier steps
Choose the branch
Pre-register metric, guardrails, end date and decision rule
Run whole weeks; no peeking
Read with compareRates and sampleRatio; label strong vs directional
exceptions_failure_modes: 2-day tests (book's meek-tweaking example) miss weekday cycles
Pooled pages hide opposite effects
Bought traffic differs from organic visitors
Lower thresholds multiply false wins across many tests
Promoting a research-backed challenger without a significant read is a judgement call, not evidence

requirements.measurement: Event on primary metric and guardrails

metrics: Primary and guardrail rates per arm
Expected false wins = tests x alpha
guardrails: No early stop on a win; harm stops allowed
No causal wording without a valid significant read
alternatives: No tracking: user tests and owner tallies
No traffic: message lab in ads (experiment-design) only if budget is approved
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: the book's 'bold not meek' rule and its low-traffic menu match ClimbOS's experiment-design skill. Two points conflict with the Microsoft ExP guide and BK06: ending at 85-90% confidence and promoting a 'research-driven' challenger at a fixed end regardless of significance. They can coexist if they are framed as pre-registered business decision rules with a directional label, which is what experiment-design SKILL.md step 8 already does.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: compute run time with sampleSize before recommending any page test; tweaks are never tested at small-business volume
proposed: a lowered decision threshold must be set before launch, applies only to reversible low-cost changes, and the readout stays 'directional'
proposed: pooled multi-page tests report a per-page direction check before claiming a pooled effect
proposed: one horizon rule across skill and code (owner horizon, default 6 weeks) instead of 6 weeks in the skill and 12 in decisions.ts

frameworks.climbos_location: PB-landing-split (shared/playbooks/contracts.ts:316-333); skills/experiment-design/SKILL.md; shared/analysis/decisions.ts sampleSize/compareRates; shared/agents/specs.ts lintExperimentFeasibility

relation_to_existing.note: Candidate v2 of PB-landing-split: computed feasibility instead of a fixed 700/week floor; adds pooled pages, bought traffic and user tests as alternatives.

frameworks.disagreements: Book part0050 [68] says ending at 90% or 85% confidence is usually worth it; 05_trustworthy_experimentation EXP-C2 and BK06 require a valid, significant read for causal wording, and compareRates defaults alpha 0.05. Book part0050 [71] would promote a research-driven challenger at a fixed end even if not winning significantly. Decider: reversibility and cost of a wrong ship. Reversible, cheap changes may use a pre-registered business threshold labelled directional; irreversible or costly ones (pricing, guarantees) keep the stricter read. The book's 2-day example duration conflicts with the whole-week rule (lint at specs.ts:878); the whole-week rule wins. Book's six-month fallback is far looser than experiment-design's ~6 weeks; ClimbOS's tighter horizon wins for small owners.

frameworks.name: Complex-sale page structure (O/CO table, commitment, modules, progressive disclosure)
frameworks.decision: How long a page should be, what the next step should ask, and how to organise many objections so visitors find answers without getting lost.
evidence_required: Objection list with counts (K2)
Counter-objections from sales, support, chat canned replies or the owner
The next step options the business can offer (trial, consult, lead magnet, purchase)
prerequisites: Confirmed facts for every counter
Mobile rendering checked (hover does not exist on touch)

branches.if: Many product-specific objections
branches.then: Build an O/CO table for one visitor type and intention, ranked by frequency

branches.if: The ask is large (contract, high price)
branches.then: Explore a lower-commitment next step (free trial, consult, lead magnet), then check persuasion is not just deferred to a later step

branches.if: Visitors differ in readiness
branches.then: Dual path: a direct low-commitment CTA plus detailed modules; CTAs repeated after objection blocks

branches.if: Visitors get lost in detail
branches.then: Modularise; headings within about three levels; spoiler headings that state the point; teaser headings only where a click is wanted

branches.if: Detail would distract from the funnel
branches.then: On-page disclosure (accordion, overlay, tooltip) instead of a new page; tap triggers on mobile

branches.if: Product has many variants
branches.then: Guide by the questions a good salesperson asks, not product codes

branches.if: Readers say 'so what?'
branches.then: Add the benefit

branches.if: Readers say 'yeah, right'
branches.then: Add the feature or other proof

branches.if: Service with an unclear after-purchase process
branches.then: Show what happens after yes, step by step

steps: Fill the O/CO table
Decide the next-step commitment
Order modules by objection frequency and where each arises
Write spoiler headings and plain copy (readability test with a real reader)
Add disclosure and fallbacks (search, FAQ, chat, phone) per economics
Test with 3-5 users on mobile
exceptions_failure_modes: Long pages fail when boring, not when long
Hidden information can conceal legally required terms
Too many equal CTAs split attention
Disclosure widgets inaccessible to keyboard or screen readers
Live chat and phone cost money and do not scale

requirements.capability: Page editor; ClimbOS drafts table and copy
requirements.measurement: Scroll/clicks on disclosures if tracked; step conversion

metrics: Clicks on primary CTA from each module
Downstream step rate (to catch deferred persuasion)
guardrails: Price, fees, cancellation and legal terms stay visible
stop_review: User tests still show the top objection unanswered: move its counter higher
Downstream drop after lowering commitment: revisit the step
alternatives: No objection data: owner's sales call notes or a recorded 7-minute pitch, transcribed
No designer: plain sections with alternating backgrounds
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: this chapter extends landing-pages with tools it lacks (O/CO table, commitment lever, progressive disclosure, heading types, future pacing, speak-first drafting). landing-pages' 'subheads that state the point' is the book's spoiler heading.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: a page brief for any offer with 5+ coded objections includes an O/CO table and names where each counter sits
proposed: progressive disclosure never hides price, mandatory fees, cancellation or other legally required terms
proposed: when a lower-commitment step is proposed, name the downstream metric that checks persuasion was not merely deferred

relation_to_existing.note: CH-C3 already says answer the prospect's questions in order; landing-pages already ties length to awareness and price. New: O/CO table, commitment lever with downstream check, disclosure patterns, heading types, future pacing.

frameworks.disagreements: landing-pages SKILL.md:116 forbids several equal-weight CTAs and prefers no navigation on paid pages; the book sometimes recommends three paths (buy, schedule trial, read more) and adding a nav tab (PhotoShelter 'Examples'). Decider: page job and traffic. Paid single-intent pages keep one primary CTA with a subordinate info path; homepages and mixed-readiness traffic can carry multiple paths.

frameworks.name: Guarantee design and safe rollout with scenario modelling
frameworks.decision: Whether to add, change or extend a guarantee, which type, and how to roll it out without unbounded refund risk.
evidence_required: Diagnosed risk or skepticism (K1/K2)
Orders per period, price, contribution per kept order, loss per invoked guarantee incl. handling
Claim period and product evaluation time
Owner confirmation the product delivers the promise
prerequisites: Owner approval; guarantee is a confirmed fact before it appears in copy (specs.ts lintOfferClaims)
Operational process for claims (returns, refunds)
Statutory rights checked (do not present legal rights as a special extra)

branches.if: Buyers fear the product won't achieve a result
branches.then: Performance guarantee

branches.if: Buyers fear they won't be happy
branches.then: Satisfaction guarantee

branches.if: Buyers fear overpaying
branches.then: Price-match guarantee

branches.if: Low price and no bold claim (the book's hot-dog example)
branches.then: No guarantee needed

branches.if: Outcome depends mainly on the customer's own effort
branches.then: Guarantee the service delivered, not the result

branches.if: Scenario grid shows loss at plausible invocation rates
branches.then: Do not launch, or narrow terms honestly

steps: Draft: name it, positive wording, matched type, easy to invoke, prompt refund, placed where risk is felt
Scenario grid in code: uplift x invocation rate -> net profit change
Short test if risk tolerance allows
Wait out the claim period
Compute actual uplift and invocation cost
Keep, extend or drop; then consider a bolder version
exceptions_failure_modes: Long feedback loop: costs known only after the claim period
Long claim periods increase exposure without more conversions
Short periods add pressure that works against the buyer
Hidden conditions destroy trust and may breach consumer law

requirements.cash: Refund reserve sized from the scenario grid
requirements.measurement: Orders and claims tagged by cohort

guardrails: No outcome guarantees the business cannot control
Statutory rights not marketed as extras
stop_review: Invocation above the break-even rate from the grid: stop or revise
alternatives: No order history: start with a narrow, low-cost satisfaction promise and a cap, labelled pilot
No test capacity: before/after over a full claim period, labelled observational
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: the nine-step rollout is a sound economic gate and maps directly to a deterministic calculator ClimbOS does not yet have (decisions.ts CalcInput lists margin, price_floor, compare_rates, sample_ratio, sample_size, before_after only). The Mobal 60-day guarantee is a reported case.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: any guarantee recommendation includes a code-computed scenario grid and break-even invocation rate
proposed: guarantees appear in copy only after the owner confirms them (already enforced for plays in specs.ts:737-746)
proposed: do not present statutory rights (e.g. distance-selling withdrawal periods where they apply) as a special guarantee

frameworks.climbos_location: New calculator kind in shared/analysis/decisions.ts; BRP-14 risk branch; skills/conversion-audit and landing-pages risk-reversal steps

relation_to_existing.note: CH-C5 picks the reducer; this adds the economics and rollout gate.

frameworks.disagreements: None material. The book's enthusiasm for 'bold' guarantees is bounded here by the scenario grid and consumer law.

frameworks.name: Offer, range and pricing levers with a compliance filter
frameworks.decision: Which offer change to make when diagnosis points to the deal (price, packaging, range) rather than clarity or trust.
evidence_required: Diagnosed offer problem with counts
Most-liked products (survey), not just best sellers
Margins (decisions.ts margin)
Visitor intentions if available (K2)
Prior selling prices with dates if any reference price is shown
prerequisites: Owner approval of any price change
Jurisdiction rules for reference prices, urgency and price testing

branches.if: Qualified buyers cite upfront cost and research shows cash constraint
branches.then: Installments or monthly billing

branches.if: Tests or research show visitors are not price-sensitive
branches.then: Add premium tiers and upsells rather than cutting price

branches.if: First purchase is not a most-liked product
branches.then: Lead with the most-liked product as the entry offer

branches.if: Many visitors want things you do not offer (gap analysis)
branches.then: Refer or partner first, build later

branches.if: Buyers anchor on price comparisons
branches.then: Compete on comparable items; earn margin on less comparable extras

branches.if: A discount is offered
branches.then: Give the genuine reason and proof

branches.if: Strike-through 'was' price requested
branches.then: Only with a genuine prior selling price meeting local rules

branches.if: Price A/B test proposed
branches.then: Check legality and fairness; book suggests charging all buyers the lower price; prefer time-based tests for legal safety

steps: Confirm the offer problem from diagnosis
Pick one lever per branch
Compute margin and break-even in code
Run through the compliance filter
Test or pilot (PB-pricing-test / PB-price-increase)
Record outcome
exceptions_failure_modes: Free can backfire as 'too good to be true'
Cheapest position is open to one competitor only
Multibuy and premiums raise refunds or support
Ad-network probes (AdSense) damage UX and brand
alternatives: No traffic for price tests: interviews with willingness-to-pay questions labelled stated, or a pilot with new customers only
No intention data: site-search logs and competitor offering scan
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: the chapter is a long idea list; its durable core is 'match the lever to the diagnosed reason' and 'the most-liked product, not the best seller, should be the entry offer'. Display tricks (decimals, odd prices) have weak evidence here and are low priority.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: a reference ('was') price requires an owner-confirmed prior selling price and period; otherwise block it
proposed: offer changes are proposed only when diagnosis names an offer problem; otherwise route to clarity, trust or readiness
proposed: gap-analysis revenue estimates are labelled assumptions and computed in code

frameworks.climbos_location: PB-pricing-test, PB-price-increase, BRP-01..06; skills/positioning; shared/analysis/decisions.ts margin/priceFloor

relation_to_existing.note: Adds the most-liked entry product, intention gap analysis and a compliance filter; pricing playbooks already exist.

frameworks.disagreements: Book endorses rolling time-limited offers (Bose) and strike-through prices; ClimbOS runtime.ts:72 bans fake urgency and specs/lint require confirmed facts. Decider: whether the deadline or prior price is genuine and confirmed.

frameworks.name: Readiness funnel, attention capture, genuine urgency and handover tracking
frameworks.decision: Whether to ask for the sale now or offer intermediate steps; how to keep not-ready visitors; how to measure when the final conversion happens elsewhere.
evidence_required: Share of visitors not ready (exit survey 'just looking' / 'need to think', or sales notes)
Buying triggers
Consented channels available
Whether the final conversion page is under the business's control
prerequisites: Consent for any contact capture and follow-up; Resend only for consented lifecycle mail
Ad budget and consent before retargeting
Tracking access on the final conversion page or a partner report

branches.if: Most visitors are browsing, early-stage
branches.then: Offer a useful intermediate step (guide, tool, email course) with consented capture (PB-lead-magnet)

branches.if: Buying is trigger-driven
branches.then: Stay remembered (follow-up, memorable name) or appear in partners' funnels at the trigger

branches.if: Visitors delay with no reason to act
branches.then: Find genuine deadlines or scarcity with a stated reason; never manufactured

branches.if: Final conversion happens on a partner page or sales team
branches.then: Persuade and qualify before handover; get conversion tracking on the true goal; optimise for completed conversions, not click-outs

branches.if: No consented audience and no budget
branches.then: Owner-led follow-up only with people who opted in; no retargeting

steps: Measure readiness mix
Design each step with a clear reward
Set consent and follow-up flow
Define the true goal metric across the handover
Review conversion per step
exceptions_failure_modes: Lead capture inflates leads but not sales
Pressure notifications erode trust and may breach consumer rules
Click-out metrics reward sending unqualified visitors

requirements.cash: $0 for owned steps; ad spend only if approved
requirements.labor: 4-12 hours to build an intermediate step
requirements.measurement: Step conversions and partner-reported final conversions

stop_review: Opt-ins rise but buyers do not within the window: revisit the step
Partner conversion data unavailable after negotiation: label click-outs as proxy
